title: Config validation: add break-glass override w/ audit logging + alert hook (admin-only)
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Adds an admin-only break-glass mechanism to bypass config validation policy gates for a single provisioning run, with mandatory reason + audit log entry.
Emits a security/ops alert hook (metric + event) when break-glass is used.
description: Context: As part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint, we are rolling out strict pool config schema + policy validation (PR #48235). Operators/SRE need an escape hatch for legitimate edge-cases (e.g., regional networking constraints, legacy customer values) without silently disabling guardrails. This PR implements the ADR-0143 break-glass mechanism: admin-only, audited, loud. What this adds: 1) Break-glass request fields: The validate/apply path now accepts an explicit `break_glass` block: `enabled: true`, `reason: <string>`, `ticket: <INT-/ENG-/SUP- key>`. Reason is required when enabled. The override is scoped to a single provisioning run (not persisted as a standing allowance). 2) Authorization: Break-glass requires the RBAC capability `fleet.config.break_glass` (admin-only). Non-admin attempts return 403 with an actionable error. The existing validation behavior remains unchanged for normal operators. 3) Audit logging: When break-glass is used, we write an immutable audit record with: actor (user/service principal), pool_id, provisioning_run_id, request_id/correlation_id, ticket, reason, validation_summary (which rules would have failed), and a config hash. This is emitted to the audit sink and is queryable via our standard audit tooling. 4) Alerting hook: We emit a structured `security_event` + metric increment `provisioning.config_validation.break_glass.count` (tagged by env/region/pool_id, with cardinality safeguards). The event includes links to the provisioning run + audit log entry. SRE/SecOps can route this to paging/ticketing via existing alert rules (follow-up: wire the actual PagerDuty policy in observability-pack). 5) UI/API ergonomics: The validation response includes `break_glass_applied: true` when used, plus the `audit_event_id` so operators can paste into incident threads. Notes/decisions: - We intentionally do NOT allow per-rule selective bypass in v1 (simple and safer): it’s “break glass for this run” and we record what would have failed. - The override does not suppress schema validation; it only bypasses policy gates (lint/policy checks) after JSON schema passes. - We require a ticket key to avoid orphaned audit entries. Related: ENG-2745 (schema + validation) and ENG-2751 (manual override flow). This also addresses INT-1047 (edge-case config blocked; request for allowlist + audit trail). Testing: Added unit tests for authz, required fields, audit payload shape, and event emission. Added an integration test that asserts policy failures can be overridden only with admin capability and that the audit record contains the failing rule IDs. Rollout: Behind existing provisioning feature flag in staging; safe to merge. No changes to default behavior unless break-glass is explicitly requested.
commits: rbac: add fleet.config.break_glass capability + enforcement in control plane handler
audit: emit config_validation_break_glass_used audit event w/ config hash + rule summary
events: add security event + metric increment w/ cardinality guardrails
tests: unit + integration coverage for override and 403 behavior
docs: update operator-facing API comments + error message hints
changed_areas: authz/rbac: capability gating and role mapping
audit logging: new event type + payload schema
review_conversation: Benji Okafor: Can we require a ticket ID in addition to reason? Otherwise we’ll get ‘test’ as a reason in prod. Jordan Lee: Added `ticket` as required when break_glass.enabled=true. Validator enforces INT-/ENG-/SUP- prefix (configurable).

Marcus Lin: Please confirm this logs to the audit sink we use for privileged actions and that it includes actor + correlation ID. Jordan Lee: Yes—emits `config_validation_break_glass_used` to AuditSink with actor principal, request_id, correlation_id, and provisioning_run_id. Added test asserting presence.

Kevin Osei: Are we risking high-cardinality metrics by tagging pool_id? Jordan Lee: Metric tags are env/region only; pool_id is included in the structured event payload (not metric labels). Response still includes audit_event_id for lookup.

Rafael Mendes: Operationally, I need the 403 error to be obvious and point to the runbook. Jordan Lee: Updated error message to include link slug `runbooks/provisioning/manual-override` and the missing capability name.

Ethan Park: Should override bypass schema validation too? We’ve seen schema failures during migrations. Jordan Lee: Not in this PR. Override is for policy gates only; schema failures are treated as hard errors to avoid undefined behavior. We can discuss adding a migration tool / versioned schema path separately (tracking in ENG-2745 follow-up).
Benji Okafor: One more request—include the list of failing rule IDs in the audit entry. Jordan Lee: Done. Audit payload includes `failed_rule_ids` and a condensed summary; tests updated.
Marcus Lin: Approving from Security provided this is admin-only and loud. Confirmed. ✅
Rafael Mendes: LGTM. This will unblock pilots without turning off guardrails. ✅
notes: Follow-up: Observability-pack alert rule tuning for break-glass events (route to ticket by default, page only on repeated use per env) will be handled separately once we have baseline volumes.
